claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Under high-strain-rate adiabatic loading, unaged HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited strain hardening, poor uniform deformability, and rapid failure.
The proposed intervention is rapid thermal aging at an optimized temperature in the range 600–800 °C for a short duration.
Rapid thermal aging of HfZrTiTa0.53 will produce a uniform dispersion of fine, coherent nanoscale B2 precipitates in its BCC matrix.
Nanoscale B2 precipitates will pin dislocations during dynamic deformation.
Precipitate-mediated dislocation pinning will increase dynamic strain hardening.
Enhanced dynamic strain hardening will delay strain localization and crack initiation.
Delayed localization and crack initiation will produce a more uniform strain distribution.
More gradual failure will reduce sudden impact-induced energy release.
Thermally aged HfZrTiTa0.53 will have a dynamic yield strength approximately 10–20% higher than the unaged baseline.
Thermally aged HfZrTiTa0.53 will exhibit a higher strain to localization under adiabatic dynamic loading.
Thermally aged HfZrTiTa0.53 will exhibit a higher fracture strain under adiabatic dynamic loading.
Thermally aged HfZrTiTa0.53 will show reduced sudden energy release during impact.
The prediction is restricted to adiabatic loading at strain rates of 10^3–10^4 s^-1.
Thermal softening is less dominant under quasi-static or moderate-strain-rate loading than under the specified high-rate loading.
A matched experiment will compare unaged and rapidly aged specimens from the same batch under identical split-Hopkinson-bar or comparable impact conditions.
Failure to obtain statistically significant gains in dynamic yield strength, uniform deformation, localization delay, and reduced energy release will falsify the hypothesis.
